Śāradā was the principal script of Kashmir for centuries, and many manuscripts from the region are written in it. Participants learn the alphabet, conjuncts and numerals, practise transliteration, and read from manuscript pages.

The course is run for your batch on dates you choose. Timings, pace and assessment are agreed before it begins.

What it covers

  • The alphabet, conjuncts and numerals
  • Practice in transliteration
  • Reading from manuscript pages

Course outline

  1. Śāradā letter practice

    Regional chronology and orthographic forms.

    You: trace alphabet

  2. Sign combinations

    Vowels, conjuncts and scribal habits.

    You: transliteration

  3. Manuscript exercise

    Legible reproduced manuscript lines.

    You: transcription

  4. Palaeographic comparison

    Late forms and editorial conventions.

    You: annotated reading

  5. Practice clinic

    Guided practice on an instructor-selected edited passage or image with vocabulary notes.

    You: correct reading and translation attempts

  6. Progress assessment

    Consolidate script/grammar patterns and discuss regional/textual variations.

    You: submit short annotated reading

The number and length of sessions are agreed with your batch.

By the end you can

  • Recognise the Śāradā alphabet, its conjuncts and its numerals.
  • Transliterate Śāradā text, taking account of vowel signs and scribal habits.
  • Read and transcribe lines from reproduced Śāradā manuscript pages.

You take away

A portfolio of your work from each session.
